qualifying_updates.title: ChatGPT scheduled tasks can trigger from Gmail, Slack, and GitHub events
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI documented event-triggered scheduled tasks that can react to supported Gmail, Slack, and GitHub events, including pull request activity such as reviews, comments, commit updates, and merges. The note states app access must be connected and approved, watched Slack channels must include the app, and event-triggered tasks cannot also use a time schedule.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Event-triggered coding or wiki-maintenance automations need source-workflow rules for app authorization, trigger coalescing, pending-event review, and GitHub activity provenance.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Record event-triggered automation as a source-workflow pattern with explicit connector permission evidence and review surfaces for batched events.

qualifying_updates.title: Codex MCP server command deprecated in favor of app server
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI marked the `codex mcp-server` command as deprecated and directed users to the Codex app server. The same changelog entry routes Claude Code usage through the Codex plugin for Claude Code.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Runtime setup instructions and MCP integration runbooks should treat command-level entry points as versioned dependencies that can be deprecated, and should separate local practice notes from upstream product documentation.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Keep agent runtime integration instructions pinned to current supported commands and capture deprecations as raw source evidence before updating durable setup leaves.

qualifying_updates.title: Runme and WebMCP notebook workflow for recurring Codex work
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI described using Runme and WebMCP to turn recurring engineering tasks into reviewable, reusable workflows. The article highlights notebooks that combine instructions, commands, results, tables, charts, Markdown, code cells, and HTML.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Reusable agent workflows can be represented as executable notebooks that preserve instructions, commands, outputs, and review context together instead of relying on one-off prompts.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Consider a local practice leaf for reviewable executable workflow artifacts where prompts, commands, generated evidence, and replay instructions are bundled for recurring tasks.

qualifying_updates.title: GitHub Copilot app Customize tab groups MCP servers, plugins, skills, and canvases
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub announced general availability of a Copilot app Customize tab that brings MCP servers, plugins, skills, and canvases into one browsing surface. The entry describes discovery by type, featured customizations, trending MCP options, and a backlog canvas for Azure DevOps triage and delegation.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Customization catalogs are becoming a practical control surface for agent tooling and context extensions; local guidance should distinguish discovery convenience from governance, approval, and scope control.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Treat customization discovery as an inventory input, not as approval; governed teams still need owner, scope, data-access, and permission records for each enabled extension.

qualifying_updates.title: Qodo Advanced Configurations for AI code review signal control
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Futurum reported that Qodo released Advanced Configurations for controlling how AI-generated code review findings are grouped, ordered, labeled, and routed into pull requests. The article says teams can configure grouping by severity, finding type, category, or relevance; use different severity label vocabularies; set truncation; route findings to inline, summary, both, or drop; and cannot drop highest-severity findings.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: AI review usefulness depends on signal routing and reviewer ergonomics, not only detection volume. Highest-severity non-droppable policies are a concrete pattern for preventing interface customization from hiding critical findings.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Capture configurable review-signal policies as a practice pattern: route low-priority findings to reduce noise while preserving mandatory surfacing for high-severity results.

qualifying_updates.title: Agentic engineering glossary defines harnesses, context, skills, evals, and workflows
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Mainmatter published a glossary for agentic engineering terms including agent harness, agent loop, context engineering, context rot, continuous AI, evals, handoff, harness engineering, hooks, plan mode, planner-generator-evaluator pattern, prompt injection, RAG, sandbox, skills, software factory, and subagent.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The glossary reflects convergence around practice vocabulary that maps closely to this wiki's local roots: context management, durable instructions, harness boundaries, subagent coordination, evaluation, and sandboxing.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use as a routing candidate for terminology normalization only where the local wiki needs practice-specific definitions; broad protocol or benchmark background belongs upstream.

qualifying_updates.title: AGNTCon and MCPCon Japan schedule centers production agent practice
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The Linux Foundation announced the AGNTCon + MCPCon Japan 2026 schedule, describing sessions on production-ready agentic AI, safe connections to tools and enterprise data, multi-agent coordination, evaluation, governance, observability, security, sandboxing, approval gates, audit trails, and verifying agent output.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The event program is evidence that production agent practice is coalescing around the same operational concerns this wiki tracks: boundaries, approvals, telemetry, evaluation, and tool safety.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Track the schedule as practice-signal evidence only; do not create local encyclopedia pages for the conference, foundation, or protocols.

qualifying_updates.title: AI governance framed as infrastructure rather than policy slides
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Improving argued that agentic AI governance should be implemented as infrastructure rather than only policy artifacts. The visible text contrasts slide-based acceptable-use governance with the need for enforceable controls.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This supports the local governance pattern that agent access, approval, audit, and enforcement must be operationalized in the runtime and workflow, not left as static policy language.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Route toward governance-controls pages as an operating-model evidence item for enforceable policy, not as broad AI governance background.

qualifying_updates.title: IANS reports AI governance visibility gaps from APIs, MCP, and plug-ins
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: IANS reported that AI governance is advancing while technical controls and visibility lag. The visible excerpt says 74 percent of enterprise AI environments pull data from external sources through APIs, MCP servers, or third-party plug-ins, expanding integrations, data paths, and identities security teams must protect.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: AI-assisted development environments inherit the same exposure pattern when coding agents connect to repositories, issue trackers, CI, package registries, databases, and local tools through plug-ins or MCP.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use as raw evidence for inventory-first governance of agent connectors, including identities and data paths introduced by developer plug-ins.

qualifying_updates.title: TrueFoundry describes per-hop guardrails for agent tool calls
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TrueFoundry described agent guardrails that inspect prompts, model outputs, MCP pre-tool calls, and MCP post-tool results. The article separates identity/access decisions from content checks, maps risks such as prompt injection, PII, secrets, destructive SQL, unsafe shell commands, and policy violations to hook points, and recommends starting guardrails in audit mode before stronger enforcement.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Per-hop inspection is a concrete runtime pattern for preventing authorized agents from acting on unsafe payloads. The audit-to-enforce rollout sequence is useful for AI-assisted development tool-call governance.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Capture the hook placement and phased enforcement approach as governed tool-call practice, while routing vendor product specifics upstream.

qualifying_updates.title: TrueFoundry frames agent systems as agent-to-loop-to-graph architecture
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TrueFoundry described a production architecture progression from single agent to durable loop to graph, then self-modification and orchestration. The article maps each step to systems questions including tool use, state, recovery, context, approvals, topology, delegation, verification, containment, promotion, and operations.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The progression provides a practice-level lens for deciding when a simple coding-agent workflow needs state externalization, graph coordination, subagent boundaries, or promotion controls.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use as candidate evidence for harness-sizing and workflow-escalation guidance: add loop and graph machinery only when state, coordination, or governance needs justify it.

qualifying_updates.title: TrueFoundry summarizes OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions for agent and MCP observability
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TrueFoundry summarized the status of OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, noting that GenAI, provider-specific, and MCP conventions moved to a dedicated repository, were marked Development, and had no official release as of August 21, 2026. The article says current concepts cover model operations, token usage, agent steps, MCP calls, content events, and evaluation results, while content capture remains opt-in and governance-sensitive.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Agent observability should pin emitted semantic versions, test backend support, separate telemetry transport from semantic maturity, and treat prompt or response capture as a policy decision rather than a default.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use as raw evidence for version-aware observability contracts, opt-in content telemetry, and separate evaluator computation from telemetry carriers.

qualifying_updates.title: Express Computer argues prompts should be managed as system logic
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Express Computer published a guest article arguing that prompts define agent behavior and should be versioned, reviewed, tested, documented, and owned. It recommends modular agent architecture, explicit contracts, validated outputs, regression tests for prompt updates, rollback paths, observability of prompt components and tool calls, and upfront automation boundaries.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The article directly supports durable-instruction practice: prompts and agent instructions should be treated as operational assets with tests, ownership, rollback, observability, and risk-scoped autonomy.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Use as evidence for prompt-change review gates and instruction ownership, not as broad agent-product coverage.
